items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (`compile_json_path_final_key`, `rhs_json_path`, `final_key`), there's a short comment on the hook, and the formatting matches the surrounding json.py code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The overridable hook is well structured and reuses `compile_json_path`. But `class HasKeyOrArrayIndex(HasKey)` is never used: KeyTransformIsNull and KeyTransformExact still call `HasKey(...)`, so the new class is dead code.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: There is no error swallowing, but the change caused a regression: integer keys meant as array indices in internal isnull paths are now quoted object keys. 6 previously passing tests now fail, e.g. test_key_transform_expression and test_nested_key_transform_on_subquery.

items.name: Array-index semantics kept for isnull / exact=None paths
items.name_zh: isnull / exact=None 路径保留数组下标语义
items.evidence: has_key, has_keys and has_any_keys are fixed in the shared code for SQLite, MySQL and Oracle. But KeyTransformIsNull.as_sqlite/as_oracle and KeyTransformExact.as_oracle still use `HasKey`, not `HasKeyOrArrayIndex`, so `__0__isnull` lookups on arrays now fail on SQLite.
